request.question: Compare the 2025 and 2026 Cedar Bay policies: annual training days in each, the increase in days and percent, and which policy supersedes which. Cite both source documents.

It is described as superseding the 2025 training policy. (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf) - Annual training allowance: 15 days per year. The table in the document shows "Annual training — 15 Days/year." (Source: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf) Numeric comparison: increase in days and percent - Raw increase in days: - 2026 days − 2025 days = 15 − 10 = 5 additional days per year. (Sources: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf; 01-policy-2025.txt) - Percent increase calculation: - Percent increase = (Increase ÷ Original amount) × 100% - Using 2025 as the original amount: (5 ÷ 10) × 100% = 0.5 × 100% = 50% - Therefore, the 2026 policy represents a 50% increase in annual training days relative to the 2025 policy. (Sources: 01-policy-2025.txt; 02-policy-2026-table.pdf) Supersession and status - The 2026 policy is explicitly marked active and is described as superseding the 2025 training policy. The 2025 policy is described as historical (Version: 2025; historical). Thus: - Which policy supersedes which: The 2026 Cedar Bay policy supersedes the 2025 Cedar Bay policy. (Source confirming supersession and active/historical status: 02-policy-2026-table.pdf; 01-policy-2025.txt) Contextual notes drawn from the documents - Both documents are labeled synthetic, fictional, and unclassified. The 2025 historical policy names Maya Chen; the 2026 active policy names Omar Patel. The 2025 document specifies its 10-day annual training allowance applies to all fictional staff; the 2026 table lists the allowance as 15 days/year.
